{{main|Tennis at the 2020 Summer Olympics}}

[[Croatia at the 2020 Summer Olympics|Croatia]]'s [[Nikola Mektić]] and [[Mate Pavić]] defeated compatriots [[Marin Čilić]] and [[Ivan Dodig]] in the final, 6–4, 3–6, [10–6] to win the gold medal in Men's Doubles [[tennis]] at the [[2020 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.itftennis.com/en/news-and-media/articles/tokyo-2020-olympics-mens-doubles-gold-medal-match/|title=Mektic and Pavic clinch men's doubles gold for Croatia|publisher=International Tennis Federation|accessdate=9 July 2025}}</ref> This was Croatia's first Olympic tennis gold and silver medals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/2020-tennis-croatias-mektic-pavic-win-mens-doubles-gold-2021-07-30/|title=Tennis-Mektic and Pavic win first tennis gold for Croatia|publisher=Reuters|accessdate=9 July 2025}}</ref> For the first time since [[Tennis at the 1908 Summer Olympics – Men's doubles|1908]], the gold medal match was contested by pairs representing the same country. In the bronze medal match, [[New Zealand at the 2020 Summer Olympics|New Zealand]]'s [[Marcus Daniell]] and [[Michael Venus (tennis)|Michael Venus]] defeated the [[United States at the 2020 Summer Olympics|United States]]' [[Austin Krajicek]] and [[Tennys Sandgren]], 7–6<sup>(7–3)</sup>, 6–2.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/sport/448137/bronze-medallists-hopeful-more-new-zealanders-will-take-up-tennis|title=Bronze medallists hopeful more New Zealanders will take up tennis|publisher=RNZ|accessdate=9 July 2025}}</ref> It was New Zealand's first Olympic tennis medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/olympics/125925474/tokyo-olympics-marcus-daniell-michael-venus-create-history-winning-bronze-medal|title=Tokyo Olympics: Marcus Daniell, Michael Venus create history winning bronze medal|publisher=Stuff|accessdate=9 July 2025}}</ref>

Spain's [[Marc López]] and [[Rafael Nadal]] were the reigning gold medalists from [[Tennis at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's doubles|2016]], but they chose not to participate.

This was the 16th (medal) appearance of the men's doubles tennis event. The event has been held at every Summer Olympics where tennis has been on the program: from 1896 to 1924 and then from 1988 to the current program. A demonstration event was held in 1968.{{cn|date=July 2021}}

The competition was a single-elimination tournament with a bronze medal match. Matches were best-of-3 sets, except that the third set was a match tiebreak (first to 10 points) instead of a typical set.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/tennis/47807003|title=Olympic men's final down to three sets|via=www.bbc.co.uk|access-date=28 December 2020|archive-date=13 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210713182306/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/tennis/47807003|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://event.itftennis.com/olympics/news//olympics/news/articles/itf-announces-changes-for-2020-olympic-tennis-event|title=Olympic Tennis Event - Tokyo 2020|website=event.itftennis.com|access-date=29 July 2021|archive-date=29 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210729121034/https://event.itftennis.com/olympics/news//olympics/news/articles/itf-announces-changes-for-2020-olympic-tennis-event|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/en/sports/tennis/|title=Tennis &#124; Olympic Sport|website=Tokyo 2020|access-date=29 July 2021|archive-date=6 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210806042248/https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/en/sports/tennis/|url-status=live}}</ref> A [[tiebreak]] was played if one of the first two sets reached 6–6.

==Qualification==
{{main|Tennis at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Qualification}}

Each [[National Olympic Committee]] (NOC) can enter up to two pairs (four players). The total number of male players, in both singles and doubles, for each nation may not exceed six. There are 32 pairs places (64 players) in the event. Qualification is based primarily on the ranking lists of 7 June 2021.<ref name=Qualifying>{{cite news|title=Tokyo 2020 – ITF Tennis Qualification System|url=https://www.itftennis.com/media/2619/qualification-system.pdf|publisher=[[International Tennis Federation|ITF]]|access-date=23 December 2020|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727092912/https://www.itftennis.com/media/2619/qualification-system.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>

Up to 10 pairs are selected through individual doubles ranking. The top 10 players in the doubles ranking qualify and may bring any partner with a ranking in the top 300 in either singles or doubles.<ref name=Qualifying/>

The draw is then filled to 24 pairs (that is, at least 14 additional pairs and possibly more depending on how the top 10 use their spots) through combined ranking. The better of a player's singles or doubles ranking is used, and the two rankings of a pair of players are added to give a combined ranking, with the lowest rankings earning qualifying spots.<ref name=Qualifying/>

If the quota of 86 total male players in singles and doubles has not been reached, the combined ranking continues until either the 86 total quota places are filled or the 32 pair maximum is reached.<ref name=Qualifying/>

Once the 86 player quota is met, priority is given to pairs with both members playing in singles (with combined ranking used to select within that group). In the unlikely event that this does not finish filling the 32 pairs, additional spots will be qualified with priority given to pairs with one member playing in singles; finally, if the 32 pair spots still are not filled, the combined ranking of pairs without any singles players is used.<ref name=Qualifying/>

==Schedule==
The competition was held over seven days from 24 July to 30 July. Times given are the start of tennis sessions, though the men's doubles shares courts with other tennis events.<ref name="Dates">{{cite web |url=https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/olympic-games/en/results/tennis/event-schedule-men-s-doubles.htm |title=Tennis - Men's Doubles Schedule |publisher=Tokyo 2020 |access-date=28 July 2021 |archive-date=28 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210728215600/https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/olympic-games/en/results/tennis/event-schedule-men-s-doubles.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>
